title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous pages: Grothendieck studies semi-simplicial ('½ simpliciaux') abelian groups that are '∂-parfaits', a fibrancy or perfection condition that makes naive Hom homotopically meaningful. He studies functors on them that are determined by their values on a small subcategory A of 'elementary' objects Φ(i,n), T_n (Eilenberg–MacLane-type pieces), and treats two cases.

This page states the conclusion for case 1 (k a Dedekind base ring) and case 2 (the generalisation, so C is the category of semi-simplicial k-modules).

Cohomological conclusion. For a (semi-)simplicial set X, set F_X(M) = Hom(X, M) = Hom(k[X], M), viewed as a functor of a perfect semi-simplicial k-module M. Knowing this functor amounts to knowing the cochain complex C^*(X, k), up to quasi-isomorphism, as an object of the derived category of k. This is Yoneda/Dold–Kan: the functor is corepresented by the chains k[X], and over a Dedekind (hereditary) ring perfect complexes are well behaved.

Main aim. Recover the extra 'multiplicative structure with divided powers' that this functor carries. Concretely:
(i) lax-monoidal maps F(M) ⊗_k F(N) → F(M ⊗ N), coming from the diagonal X → X × X (f, g ↦ x ↦ f(x) ⊗ g(x), degreewise);
(ii) divided-power maps Γ^i F(M) → F(Γ^i M), f ↦ γ_i ∘ f degreewise.
He wants these read as cochain-level structures on C^* = C^*(X, k): a commutative-up-to-coherence algebra structure with divided powers.

Open question, continued on the next page:
- In characteristic 0 this structure should be determined by Sullivan's de Rham complex of polynomial forms.
- In general it should be determined by 'de Rham complexes with divided powers', in the style of H. Cartan's 1976 'Théories cohomologiques'.
- Ultimately: to what extent does C^* with its divided-power multiplicative structure reconstruct the homotopy type of X? This is integral or p-adic 'algebraic models of homotopy types', the question later answered by Mandell (E∞ cochains) and approached by Toën (affine stacks / cosimplicial algebras).
errors: No outright error, but there is a gap. Semi-simplicial objects have no degeneracies, so the degreewise tensor product M ⊗ N and the degreewise Γ^i are not obviously homotopically meaningful: Eilenberg–Zilber and Dold–Puppe derived functors use degeneracies. One must check that '∂-perfect' and the dévissage make F(M) ⊗ F(N) → F(M ⊗ N) and Γ^i F → F Γ^i well defined up to homotopy. The page does not address this.
The claim that the functor M ↦ Hom(X, M) 'is equivalent to' C^*(X, k) is stated without the qualifier 'up to quasi-isomorphism / in D(k)'. It is presumably intended, possibly in the illegible phrase.

ideas.what: The functor M ↦ Hom(X, M) on (fibrant/perfect) semi-simplicial k-modules encodes exactly the cochain complex C^*(X, k) in D(k).
ideas.modern_name: Corepresentability by chains k[X]; Dold–Kan / Yoneda in the derived category
ideas.where_published: Analogous viewpoint in Pursuing Stacks (1983), on abelianisation and Hom into simplicial abelian groups

ideas.what: Encode the multiplicative structure of cochains as natural transformations F(M) ⊗ F(N) → F(M ⊗ N) and Γ^i F(M) → F(Γ^i M), i.e. as 'functor with products and divided powers' structure.
ideas.modern_name: E∞ / cosimplicial-commutative-algebra structure on cochains with divided powers; dually, k[X] as a simplicial cocommutative coalgebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartan (1976, divided-power de Rham); Mandell (2001, 2006, E∞ cochains); Toën (2006, affine stacks)
ideas.where_published: Related ideas in Grothendieck's 1975 letters to L. Breen and in Pursuing Stacks (schematisation of homotopy types); not this functorial formulation as far as known

ideas.what: Programme (continued on next page): the structure is determined by Sullivan's de Rham complex rationally, and by de Rham complexes with divided powers integrally; ask whether C^* with this structure recovers the homotopy type of X.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic models of integral/p-adic homotopy types
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977, rational); Cartan (1976); Cenkl–Porter (1980s); Mandell (2001 p-adic, 2006 integral); Toën (2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks / letters to Breen discuss schematic homotopy types; uncertain whether this exact formulation appears

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks, c. 1975–76, whether cochains C^*(X, k) with multiplicative and divided-power structure (packaged functorially via Hom(X, −) on perfect semi-simplicial k-modules over a Dedekind ring) determine the homotopy type of X. This anticipates by ~25 years Mandell's theorem that E∞ cochains determine finite-type nilpotent homotopy types. The specific route — dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules into elementary pieces, then structure maps on the functor — is apparently not in the literature.
missed.quote: Notre propos principal a été ici essentiellement reconstituer la structure multiplicative "puissances divisées" sur ce foncteur M ↦ F_X(M) = Hom(X, M) ... en tant que structures de cochaînes sur le complexe C^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers an early, Dedekind-base, functor-of-points formulation of the 'cochain algebras determine homotopy types' problem. It is close in spirit to Toën's affine stacks and to Lurie/Mandell. Its main interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck reached the integral question independently around the time of Cartan's divided-power de Rham work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic summary, not a new theorem. The question it raises (E∞ / divided-power cochains as an integral model of homotopy types) is now well known (Cartan 1976, Mandell, Toën) and was in the air via Sullivan and Cartan in 1975–76. The specific formulation via divided-power structure maps on Hom(X, −) over ∂-perfect semi-simplicial modules is a notable unpublished detail, but it is only mildly surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'La dérivation [?] cohomologique [?] à retenir' is more likely 'La conclusion cohomologique à retenir'.
'la structure multiplicative "par dessus" [?]' should almost certainly read 'la structure multiplicative à "puissances divisées"' (consistent with Γ^i and with 'à p.d.' on the next page).
'k-modules sth. [?]' likely means 'k-modules ½ s.' (semi-simplicial), with 'parfaits' inserted.
'(comme fonction de M)' is probably 'comme foncteur en M'.
'; resp. dans [?] k' is likely a qualifier such as 'à quasi-isom. près, dans D(k)'; illegible.

Last line: 'Il faudrait examiner si par le cas o' probably reads 'Il faudrait examiner si, dans le cas où car k = 0, ces structures supplémentaires' (leading to 'est déterminé par le complexe de De Rham–Sullivan' on the next page).
